📡 Threat Intelligence Feed Matches
spec.description: IOC stands for Indicator of Compromise. In cybersecurity, an IOC is a piece of forensic data or digital evidence that identifies malicious activity or a network breach.In your dashboard's "Threat Intelligence Feed Matches" panel, ioc_type (which the panel maps to display as "IOC Category") specifies the exact format of the malicious evidence that your engine intercepted.  Your engine categorizes these hits into three specific ioc_type values:  domain: A device on your network attempted to look up a malicious website name (e.g., evil-c2-server.com) that is explicitly blocked by your threat intelligence feeds.  ip: A device attempted a direct network connection to a dangerous numeric IP address flagged by reputation databases like AbuseIPDB.  mixed: A multi-vector flag where advanced tools like VirusTotal found malicious associations with both the requested domain and its destination IP address.

spec.title: 🤖 Autonomous False-Positive Elimination Engine (CL-AFPE) — Real-Time Triage & Self-Healing

options.content:
### 🤖 **CL-AFPE Autonomous Triage Engine**
Intercepts alert breaches (`risk >= 6.0`) before Telegram notification and evaluates them through a 3-stage pipeline:
* **Stage 1 (Hard-Stop):** ThreatIntel IOC, JA3/JA4+, Lateral Movement, Honeypot access
* **Stage 2 (LightGBM ONNX):** Tabular $P(\text{FP})$ classifier on Tranco rank, label entropy, Z-score, device type
* **Stage 3 (FastEmbed Vector Match):** Cosine similarity against 50+ safe vendor patterns (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5)
